R689.note: Canonicalised base plus resolve/normalize/startsWith and a second toRealPath containment check closes traversal and symlink escape; the displayed fileName becomes the real path and the not-found error text changes wording, but both are identical in the ordinary case.

R690.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes' => false]) keeps the wire format and blocks object instantiation; is_array guard preserves the empty-cart fallback and array shape per the contract (no HMAC added, but the sink-level fix is the appropriate one).

R691.note: enable_shared_from_this with self = shared_from_this() capture and make_shared in the only caller keeps the Widget alive until the queued task runs; the shared_ptr-ownership precondition is stated and only forbids the pattern that was the bug.

R692.note: SqlParameter @ownerName replaces string.Format; same single DELETE, same row-count branching.

R693.note: pool.execute with a ? placeholder binds userId as data; result set and error handling unchanged for numeric ids.

R694.note: encode_entities on both tainted values at their element-text insertion points; static badge untouched.

R695.note: {0} filterArgs form lets JNDI escape the value; new SearchControls() is documented as equivalent to the original null cons.

R696.note: jwt.verify with a pinned algorithms list closes the unsigned-token path; the new JWT_SECRET requirement and the HS256 assumption are both stated plainly with the follow-up needed if tokens are asymmetric.

R699.note: Re-indexing tasks[activeIndex] after push_back removes the dangling reference; observable state after the call is identical.

R700.note: token.Method type assertion plus WithValidMethods closes algorithm confusion, but pinning to HS256 only is narrower than the stated HMAC-secret contract (HS384/HS512 tokens signed with the same secret would now be rejected) and the write-up does not flag that assumption.
